skill.name: caveman
skill.description: Ultra-compressed communication mode for terse technical replies. It removes filler and pleasantries while preserving technical accuracy and clear safety warnings.
skill.summary: Compress technical responses while keeping facts, warnings, and code intact.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and a fenced SQL example in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or executable shell behavior was found in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"
> Inline obj prop -> new ref -> re-render. `useMemo`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 22 uses Markdown backticks to describe a response pattern, not Ruby or shell execution. It contains no command invocation or user-controlled execution path.

content.user_title: Compress Technical Replies With Caveman Mode
content.value_statement: Long assistant replies can waste attention and context budget. This skill makes Claude, Codex, and Claude Code answer tersely while preserving technical meaning.
actual_capabilities: Turns assistant responses into terse technical fragments after activation.
Removes filler words, pleasantries, hedging, and extra transitions.
Keeps exact technical terms, code blocks, and error messages unchanged.
Uses arrows and abbreviations for compact cause and effect explanations.
Temporarily expands wording for security warnings and irreversible actions.
limitations: It changes response style only and does not add new tool access.
It may feel too terse for onboarding, teaching, or stakeholder updates.
It depends on explicit stop commands to return to normal style.
It does not shorten code blocks or exact quoted errors.

use_cases.title: Speed Up Debugging Chats
use_cases.description: Get compact root-cause notes, fixes, and next steps while working through technical issues.

use_cases.title: Reduce Context Usage
use_cases.description: Keep long Claude, Codex, or Claude Code sessions concise when context budget matters.

use_cases.title: Create Brief Technical Summaries
use_cases.description: Convert analysis into short, precise updates for pull requests, tickets, or review notes.

prompt_templates.title: Enable Caveman Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Use caveman mode for this session. Keep technical accuracy, but remove filler and pleasantries.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Briefly
prompt_templates.scenario: Ask for a compact explanation of a concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this in caveman mode: [paste concept, error, or design]. Keep key terms exact.

prompt_templates.title: Debug With Minimal Tokens
prompt_templates.scenario: Get a short diagnosis and fix path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Caveman mode. Diagnose this issue and give likely cause, fix, and next check: [paste details].

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Technical Findings
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce a terse status update from detailed analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use caveman mode to summarize these findings for engineers. Include impact, root cause, fix, and risk: [paste notes].

output_examples.input: Explain why this React component keeps rendering.
output_examples.output: Prop object recreated each render. Child sees new ref -> rerender. Memoize object or move it outside render.

output_examples.input: Summarize this failed deploy for the backend team.
output_examples.output: Deploy failed at migration step. Missing index blocks query plan. Add index, rerun migration, verify rollback path.

output_examples.input: Warn me before a destructive database action.
output_examples.output: Warning: action deletes user rows permanently. Confirm backup exists and rollback plan is tested before running it.

best_practices: Use it when you need dense technical answers, not broad teaching.
Ask for normal mode when clarity matters more than brevity.
Keep safety warnings explicit, even when the rest of the response is terse.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for sensitive stakeholder communication that needs careful tone.
Do not use it when a beginner needs step-by-step context.
Do not shorten legal, security, or destructive-action warnings beyond clear meaning.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It makes assistant replies much shorter while keeping technical substance, exact code, and important warnings intact.

faq.question: How do I activate it?
faq.answer: Ask for caveman mode, talk like caveman, use caveman, be brief, or less tokens.

faq.question: How do I turn it off?
faq.answer: Say stop caveman or normal mode. The skill is designed to persist until you ask it to stop.

faq.question: Does it change code?
faq.answer: No. The instructions say code blocks and exact error text should stay unchanged.

faq.question: Will it hide safety warnings?
faq.answer: No. It temporarily expands wording for security warnings, irreversible actions, and sequences where terse fragments may confuse.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
